_readme: Vocabulary list for eval/eval_generation.py's unglossed-jargon metric.
`needs_gloss` seeds from the Translation rule's own list in test_rag_compare.py's
SYSTEM_PROMPT (posterior pelvic tilt, lordotic, knee extension moment, plantar flexors,
biarticular, hypertrophy, brachii, muscular complex, kinematic, medial knee displacement,
supinated, ...), then adds the terms that actually leaked into compare_result_v9.md but the
prompt never named (hip abduction, external rotation, gluteus, femur, spinal). Keeping the
list here rather than parsing it out of the prompt is deliberate: the metric has to be able
to flag a term the prompt FORGOT to list - that is the whole point of measuring.
`allowed_bare` is the prompt's own 'you may use these with no explanation' list plus terms
that are ordinary gym-floor English (rep, set, range of motion). Anything here is never
flagged, even if a needs_gloss entry is a substring of it.
Error names from the session JSON ('Knee valgus', 'Butt wink') are NOT listed here - the
script reads them out of the report's own Retrieval metrics table per exercise, because the
prompt REQUIRES the model to use the session's error names verbatim. Flagging those would
penalise the model for obeying an instruction.
`gloss_markers` are the shapes an in-sentence explanation takes in this report format. A
term counts as glossed when a marker follows it within `window` characters in the same
sentence, or when the term itself sits inside a parenthetical after plain words.
Editing this file changes the numbers. Say which revision produced a number when you quote
one, the same way a golden-set score names its collection.
